body: From what you posted I can see you are not running the latest version of syncthing everywhere. Upgrade everywhere first drop a note if it still happens and we will reopen.
.17 or .18 shouldn't matter here. This looks like a real problem to me. Possibly same as #3764 and I wonder if symlinks on Windows work at all and if anyone at all uses that feature...
I suspect one of the nodes participating is pre-symlink field, and uses blocks instead, hence permanently bounces as one stores it the field, other stores in the block.

The version information is in my opinion clear enough, to know how version i use and it's clear to me, that an upgrade can possible clear some problems, if new updates available.

I had the problem with .17 and have it now also with .18

With .14 i have also delete this symlinks and created new.
I am not talking about a single version, I am talking about all devices involved. The fact that changes come from unknown device imply an old version.
No, all devices use .18. And if i make a change on a windows device, in global changes it shows, that it come from the windows device, but not for the symlink problem.
I'm fairly sure this is a genuine bug so we can stop doubting @n86io :) There is code to prevent sending new format symlink entries to old versions, even.
Yet I am still suspicious about the unset ModifiedBy in the screenshots.
Sorry @AudriusButkevicius, but i have no reason, to mislead you or other developers and i have no time for such silly things. ;-)

I'm having a hard time duplicating this:

Client 1:   Windows 10  14393.576 + ST v0.14.18
Client 2:   Windows 10  14393.576 + ST v0.14.18

When I make either dir or regular symlink on either client I get no sync of any file and no mention of it in the log.  ST just ignores them, which I understand to be the correct behavior.

Maybe problem is between Windows and Linux?

Or maybe I'm misunderstanding whats wrong here?

Syncthing probably needs to run as administrator to sync the symlinks. If it does that, the links should sync properly in Windows as well.

(I suspect they won't, but they *should*.)
Yes it's right. Only if syncthing run as administrator symlinks will be sync. On this way i've made it. But because of the problem i have currently ignored the symlinks and created on each device.

Ok so I have it reproducing now... when I create symlink on Windows (using mklink.exe at the admin CLI) I get a symlink (surprise), but... on first sync it makes a .symlink file on the other windows box, which is not recognized as a symlink... just a plain file that is a type .symlink.  Windows parses filnames in filename.ext format so maybe it's just getting confused that there is nothing before the dot and so thinking thats the filetype.

Whatever... anyway, after that the next scan, few secs later (on the receiver) it then resyncs that file back clobbering the original valid symlink with this .symlink file so they both have the crappy non working one.

And yes it says device unknown and modified in log for both direction syncs.  Of course that's prob cause we set it too use that for blank or invalid ID.
Unknown is for blank, but it should never be blank.

Wow, this is broken. I figured I'd test this out. - Started my Win10 - Command prompt as administrator - `mkdir c:\test1` - `cd c:\test1` - `mklink /d link1 c:\Windows` - Start a new blank syncthing instance, 0.14.18 downloaded from github - Add `c:\test1` as a folder, figured I'd see what it adds to the index and then see what gets synced It follows the shit out of that symlink...
It follows as it's at the root, so it makes sense.
It's not at the root
A file type symlink towards something that does not exist gets synced correctly, but the global log looks like @nrm21 says (type "file" even).
Ah yes, it's not at the root. Regarding Unknown I suspect we are not setting ModifiedBy somewhere.
And yes, following the link... Wtf.

Wow, this is *really* weird. I created a recursive directory symlink, `c:\test1\dir\recursive -> c:\test1`, and 1. Syncthing follows it, gets infinite recursion and breaks the sync 2. `dir /s` also does infinite recursion until it breaks I poke around a little, and now `dir /s` does *not* do recursion any more. Look at it closely, the symlink type has changed from `SYMLINKD` to `SYMLINK` and is not followed. Create another one with `mklink /d` and we're back in recursion land.
